changes.from: **Over time.** A level rests on several pieces of evidence, and the strongest reading from this school year stands. One good day or one hard day never decides it.
changes.to: **Over time.** A level rests on a pattern across several observations from this school year. One good day or one hard day never decides it.

changes.from: Choose the measure the evidence shows most clearly.
changes.to: Choose the one or two measures the evidence shows most clearly.

changes.from: - **The moment comes first.** We never stop a child's play or work to test a measure. Educators watch, listen and document, and read the evidence afterward.
changes.to:
- **The moment comes first.** We never stop a child's play or work to test a measure. Educators watch, listen and document, and read the evidence afterward.
- **One observation, two measures at most.** TREE offers up to four measures to choose from, and one observation counts toward no more than two for a child.
- **The observation stays as written.** Educators never change an observation or their image of the child to fit a measure. The measure is read from the observation.

changes.from: Small group happens twice a day. In the morning it begins soon after arrival, once every member of the group has arrived. In the afternoon it runs until the class comes back together. The same educator stays with the same group for the whole sitting, without interruption.
changes.to: Small group is scheduled in the morning, most often Tuesday to Friday. It can come together again at any time of day when the children's interests and needs call for it. The same educator stays with the same group for the whole sitting, without interruption.

changes.from: The new educator has a go-to person for everyday questions. The mentor works alongside that person and the director, and stays close to the practice itself, in the room with children.
changes.to: Every new educator has a go-to person, the first one they turn to with any question in their first weeks. They also learn beside an experienced educator in their class, who mentors them on the floor and stays close to the practice itself. Sometimes one person holds both roles. Both work alongside the director.
